title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 66 (Reduction of share capital)

content.overview: A company limited by shares or a company limited by guarantee and having share capital may reduce its share capital by special resolution, subject to confirmation by the Tribunal, creditor protections, accounting-standard requirements and the statutory bar relating to arrears of deposits or interest.
content.glance: A company limited by shares or a company limited by guarantee and having share capital may reduce its share capital by special resolution, subject to confirmation by the Tribunal, creditor protections, accounting-standard requirements and the statutory bar relating to arrears of deposits or interest.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 66 (Reduction of share capital). A company limited by shares, or a company limited by guarantee and having share capital, may reduce its share capital by special resolution, subject to confirmation by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). The reduction may include extinguishing or reducing liability on unpaid share capital, cancelling paid-up capital lost or unrepresented by available assets, or paying off paid-up capital that is in excess of the company's wants. The Tribunal considers creditor protection and may require consent, discharge, determination or security for creditor claims as the section provides. The company must give notice to the Central Government, Registrar, SEBI where applicable and creditors as directed, and comply with accounting-standard and filing requirements. A reduction must not be confirmed where the company is in arrears in repayment of deposits or interest, subject to the statutory wording. This is a capital-reduction procedure, distinct from buy-back under section 68.

sections.heading: Eligible company and approval
sections.body: A company limited by shares, or a company limited by guarantee and having share capital, may reduce share capital by special resolution, subject to NCLT confirmation.

sections.heading: Permitted forms of reduction
sections.body: A reduction may extinguish or reduce liability on unpaid share capital, cancel paid-up share capital lost or unrepresented by available assets, or pay off paid-up share capital in excess of the company's wants.

sections.heading: Creditor protection and notices
sections.body: The Tribunal considers creditor claims and the statutory safeguards. Notice is given to the Central Government, Registrar, SEBI where applicable and creditors as directed; creditor consent, discharge, determination or security must be addressed as required by the section and Tribunal process.

sections.heading: Statutory bar and accounting standards
sections.body: The section restricts confirmation where the company is in arrears in repayment of deposits or interest, subject to the statutory wording. The company must comply with applicable accounting standards and provide any required auditor certificate.

sections.heading: Order and filing
sections.body: After confirmation, comply with the requirements for filing the Tribunal order and approved minute with the Registrar within the statutory period. Verify the current rules/forms and deadline before filing.

sections.heading: Distinction from buy-back
sections.body: Section 66 is a Tribunal-confirmed reduction of share capital; section 68 is a buy-back procedure with different funding, limits and process conditions.

examples.title: Selective reduction
examples.body: A reduction extinguishing a class on fair terms still needs special resolution and NCLT confirmation.

examples.title: Deposit default
examples.body: A company in default of deposit repayment cannot use reduction to return paid-up capital except as s. 66 permits.

hypotheticals.question: A company proposes to cancel paid-up capital lost or unrepresented by available assets. What process applies?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 66 permits that form of reduction, but the company must pass a special resolution and obtain NCLT confirmation, while satisfying creditor protections, accounting-standard requirements and the statutory bar.

hypotheticals.question: A company has arrears in repayment of deposits or interest. Can it obtain confirmation of a capital reduction?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 66 contains a statutory restriction on confirmation where the company is in arrears in repayment of deposits or interest. Check the current text and any applicable statutory qualification before proceeding.

distinctions.left: Section 66 reduces share capital through special resolution and NCLT confirmation.
distinctions.right: Section 68 purchases own shares/securities under a separate buy-back procedure.

misconceptions.trap: Saying section 66 prohibits extinguishing liability on unpaid share capital.
misconceptions.correction: Extinguishing or reducing liability on unpaid share capital is one of the forms of reduction expressly contemplated by section 66.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a special resolution alone as sufficient.
misconceptions.correction: NCLT confirmation, creditor protection and the applicable accounting-standard and filing requirements also apply.

misconceptions.trap: Treating capital reduction as the same transaction as a buy-back.
misconceptions.correction: Section 66 reduction and section 68 buy-back are distinct statutory procedures.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the forms of reduction identified in section 66?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: They include extinguishing or reducing liability on unpaid share capital, cancelling paid-up capital lost or unrepresented by available assets, and paying off paid-up capital in excess of the company's wants.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is a special resolution alone sufficient?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. NCLT confirmation and statutory creditor, accounting and filing requirements must also be met.
